belief: Struggling financially means I'm out of God's will.
origins: Many believers equate being in God’s will with everything falling into place. When a job ends or money gets tight, they wonder if they missed a turn. A past decision, such as a career move, a risky purchase, or an act of disobedience, can seem to be the cause, and the worry becomes a constant question: “Did I get out of God’s will?”
teaches: Scripture says, “I know the plans I have for you, declares the LORD, plans to prosper you and not to harm you, to give you a future and a hope.” Proverbs says, “A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.” The psalmist says, “The steps of a man are ordered by the LORD… Though he falls, he will not be overwhelmed, for the LORD is holding his hand.” Paul, who was in God’s will, was shipwrecked, imprisoned, and often in need. Hardship does not prove we have wandered off the path.
self_statements: I must have missed God’s direction.
This is what happens when I step out of His will.
If I were in His will, things would be smoother.
I made a wrong turn and ruined everything.
God is not guiding me anymore.
I cannot trust my own decisions.
errors: Judging past decisions by results I could not know.
Believing I am either perfectly in God’s will or out of it.
Feeling lost and concluding that I am out of His will.
Blaming myself for circumstances with many causes.
questions: What exactly do I believe I did that took me out of God’s will?
Did people in the Bible who followed God face hardship? What does that say?
What does God promise about directing my steps?
Is there any known disobedience I need to confess, and what does Scripture say about forgiveness?
What good has God brought out of past hard times?
What is one next faithful step?
truth: God orders the steps of those who follow Him, and when I fall, He holds my hand. Hardship does not prove I am out of His will. I can confess any sin, take the next faithful step, and trust Him to work all things for good.
hw_truths: He holds my hand when I fall.
His plans for me are for a future and a hope.

log: Each day, write one faithful step you can take today.
actions: Describe the decision you fear took you out of God’s will.

prayer: Lord, You hold my hand. Forgive me where I have strayed, and guide me where I am confused. Order my steps, and help me trust that You are with me in hard times. Amen.
